answer: The advantage in BA-completion rates for Black students is most pronounced at the HIGHEST socioeconomic level. Overall, and across the low- and middle-SES quintiles, Black students complete at a LOWER rate than White students (Black 0.2–2.2% vs White 1.3–4.2%). The Black–White gap steadily narrows as SES rises and effectively closes at the top: in the top SES quintile Black completion (7/203 = 3.45%) essentially equals White (50/1416 = 3.53%), and in the top SES decile Black completion (5/82 = 6.10%) is the highest of any group, exceeding both White (36/737 = 4.88%) and Hispanic (2/58 = 3.45%). This high-SES advantage is robust in direction: in a logistic model controlling for ASVAB ability, class percentile, and sex, the Black × top-SES interaction is the single largest positive effect (OR ≈ 8, p ≈ 0.07), and it holds even though high-SES Black students have lower mean ability than high-SES White students (ASVAB ≈ 1945 vs ≈ 2224). Caveat, stated plainly: the top-level "advantage" rests on very few completions — 5 of 82 Black students in the top decile (SE ≈ ±2.6 pp) and 7 of 203 in the top quintile (SE ≈ ±1.3 pp) — so the point estimate is imprecise and its confidence interval includes zero. The defensible reading is that the Black–White completion gap is at its smallest, effectively closed and modestly positive in the raw data, precisely at the highest SES level; that is where any Black-student advantage is concentrated.

payload.workflow: 1) Load data/nls_ses_processed.csv (N=8773, 0 missing); confirm SES is a continuous standardized-ish score (mean -0.009, std 0.742, range -2.445..2.718) and BA DEGREE COMPLETED a clean binary. 2) Define completion rate = mean(BA DEGREE COMPLETED); overall 2.69% (White 3.54%, Black 1.33%, Hispanic 1.44%). 3) Segment SES into quintiles (primary) and deciles (robustness) via quantile cuts. 4) For each SES bin compute Black vs White (primary comparator), Black vs Hispanic, and Black vs overall-mean completion gaps in pp plus ratios, reporting per-cell N and raw counts (s/n) and a Wald SE for the Black cell. 5) Identify the SES level where the Black advantage is largest/positive. 6) Sensitivity (not in headline): fit logistic regression completion ~ SES-quintile + race + SES-quintile:race + ASVAB ability + class percentile + sex to test whether the high-SES Black advantage survives covariate adjustment (it does, directionally; Black x top-SES is the largest positive interaction, OR~8, p~0.07). Concluded the advantage is most pronounced at the highest SES level, with the caveat that the top-cell estimate is imprecise.
